# varunayan

> Python toolkit for downloading and processing climate reanalysis and observational data. Built with a focus on India, but supports global datasets.

varunayan provides access to ERA5 reanalysis, IMD gridded observations, HadEX3 climate extremes indices, and CRU TS monthly climate grids. It includes heat stress index calculations (UTCI, WBGT, Heat Index, Humidex), country-level temperature aggregation, ERA5 variable discovery, spatial analysis utilities, and a download cache.

## Data Sources

- ERA5: Global reanalysis from ECMWF/Copernicus CDS. 0.25 degree grid, hourly, 1940-present. Single-level and pressure-level datasets. Access via bounding box, point coordinates, or GeoJSON polygon.
- IMD: India Meteorological Department gridded data. Rainfall at 0.25 degree (NetCDF), temperature (tmax/tmin/tmean) at 1 degree (binary .grd), 1901-present.
- HadEX3: Hadley Centre global ETCCDI climate extremes indices. 1.875 degree grid. Annual and monthly frequencies.
- CRU TS: Climatic Research Unit (v4.07) monthly climate grids. 0.5 degree, 1901-present. Variables: tmp, pre, vap, pet, tmn, tmx, dtr, wet, frs, cld, rhm.

## Installation

```
pip install varunayan
```

Requires Python 3.10+. ERA5 downloads require a CDS API key (auto-configured on first use).

## Modules and API

### ERA5 Core (`varunayan.core`)

```python
from varunayan import era5ify_bbox, era5ify_point, era5ify_geojson

era5ify_bbox(request_id="demo", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
era5ify_point(request_id="point", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", latitude=28.6, longitude=77.2)
era5ify_geojson(request_id="geo", variables=["2m_temperature"], start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", json_file="region.geojson", dist_features=["state"])
```

Common parameters: `dataset_type` ("single" or "pressure"), `pressure_levels` (list of strings like ["1000","850"]), `frequency` ("hourly","daily","weekly","monthly","yearly"), `resolution` (grid spacing in degrees, default 0.25), `verbosity` (0/1/2), `save_raw` (bool).

### ERA5 Variable Discovery (`varunayan.search_and_desc`)

```python
from varunayan import search_variable, list_available_variables, describe_variables, list_variable_categories, get_variable_info, get_variable_units, get_variable_long_name, get_available_pressure_levels

search_variable("temperature")
list_available_variables(dataset_type="single")
list_variable_categories(dataset_type="single")
describe_variables(["2m_temperature", "total_precipitation"], dataset_type="single")
get_variable_info("2m_temperature", dataset_type="single")
get_variable_units("2m_temperature", dataset_type="single")
get_variable_long_name("2m_temperature", dataset_type="single")
get_available_pressure_levels()
```

### ERA5 Convenience (`varunayan.convenience`)

One-call wrappers that download ERA5 data and return processed DataFrames.

```python
from varunayan import get_era5_daily_temperature, get_era5_daily_humidity, get_era5_daily_wind, get_era5_daily_heat_index_data, get_era5_monthly_heat_index_data, get_era5_daily_heat_index_geojson, get_era5_daily_heat_index_point

df = get_era5_daily_temperature(request_id="t", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_humidity(request_id="h", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_wind(request_id="w", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = get_era5_daily_heat_index_data(request_id="hi", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
```

### IMD (`varunayan.imd`)

```python
from varunayan import (
    download_imd_rainfall, download_imd_temperature,
    read_imd_rainfall, read_imd_temperature,
    imd_rainfall_bbox, imd_rainfall_geojson,
    imd_temperature_bbox, imd_temperature_geojson,
    process_imd_files, filter_imd_by_bbox, filter_imd_by_geojson,
    aggregate_imd_by_frequency,
    list_imd_datasets, get_imd_grid_specs,
)

# Download raw files
download_imd_rainfall(start_year=2020, end_year=2023)
download_imd_temperature(start_year=2020, end_year=2023, variable="tmax")

# Read downloaded files into DataFrames
df = read_imd_rainfall(file_path="path.nc", resolution=0.25, year=2020)
df = read_imd_temperature(file_path="path.grd", var_type="tmax", year=2020)

# One-call pipelines: download + read + crop
df = imd_rainfall_bbox(request_id="r", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = imd_temperature_bbox(request_id="t", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0, variable="tmax")
df = imd_rainfall_geojson(request_id="rg", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, geojson_file="region.geojson")
df = imd_temperature_geojson(request_id="tg", start_year=2020, end_year=2020, geojson_file="region.geojson", variable="tmax")

# Post-processing
df = filter_imd_by_bbox(data=df, north=28.7, south=28.5, east=77.3, west=77.0)
df = aggregate_imd_by_frequency(data=df, frequency="monthly", variable="rainfall")

# Metadata
list_imd_datasets()
get_imd_grid_specs("rainfall_0.25")
```

IMD temperature variable options: "tmax", "tmin", "tmean".

### IMD Stations (`varunayan.imd_stations`)

```python
from varunayan import get_imd_stations

stations = get_imd_stations(with_coordinates=True, max_workers=8)
```

Returns a DataFrame of IMD observation stations with optional lat/lon lookup.

### HadEX3 (`varunayan.hadex3`)

```python
from varunayan import hadex3_bbox, hadex3_geojson, list_hadex3_indices

indices = list_hadex3_indices(frequency="all")
df = hadex3_bbox(index="TXx", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, north=35, south=8, east=90, west=68)
df = hadex3_geojson(index="TXx", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, geojson_file="india.geojson")
```

Available ETCCDI indices: TXx, TNn, TX90p, TN10p, FD, SU, TR, WSDI, CSDI, DTR, ETR, GSL, Rx1day, Rx5day, SDII, R10mm, R20mm, R95p, R99p, PRCPTOT, CDD, CWD. Some indices have both annual and monthly frequency.

### CRU TS (`varunayan.cru_ts`)

```python
from varunayan import cru_ts_bbox, cru_ts_geojson, list_cru_ts_variables

variables = list_cru_ts_variables()
df = cru_ts_bbox(variable="tmp", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, north=35, south=8, east=90, west=68)
df = cru_ts_geojson(variable="tmp", start_year=2000, end_year=2020, geojson_file="india.geojson")
```

Valid variables: tmp (temperature), pre (precipitation), vap (vapor pressure), pet (potential evapotranspiration), tmn (min temperature), tmx (max temperature), dtr (diurnal temperature range), wet (wet days), frs (frost days), cld (cloud cover), rhm (relative humidity).

### Country-Level Temperature (`varunayan.country`)

```python
from varunayan import get_era5_country_temperature

df = get_era5_country_temperature(country="India", start_date="2023-06-01", end_date="2023-06-30", variables="mean")
```

Parameters: `country` (name string or GeoDataFrame), `variables` ("mean", "max", "min", or list). Uses Natural Earth boundaries with cosine-latitude area weighting. Works for any country, not just India.

### Heat Stress Indices (`varunayan.heat_stress`)

```python
from varunayan import (
    utci, utci_sparse, utci_category,
    wbgt_simple, wbgt_shade, wbgt_outdoor, wbgt_risk_category,
    heat_index, heat_index_from_dewpoint, heat_index_risk_category,
    humidex,
    mean_radiant_temperature,
    wet_bulb_temperature, wet_bulb_from_dewpoint,
    relative_humidity_from_dewpoint, vapor_pressure_from_dewpoint,
    calc_heat_indices,
)

# UTCI: Universal Thermal Climate Index (Bröde polynomial approximation)
utci_val = utci(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0, wind_ms=2.0, mrt_c=50.0)
category = utci_category(utci_val)

# UTCI sparse: Legendre polynomial (Roman et al. 2025, wider wind range)
utci_val = utci_sparse(temp_c=35.0, tmrt=50.0, wind_speed=2.0, rh=60.0)

# WBGT variants
wbgt_val = wbgt_simple(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
wbgt_val = wbgt_shade(temp_c=35.0, wet_bulb_c=28.0)
wbgt_val = wbgt_outdoor(temp_c=35.0, wet_bulb_c=28.0, globe_temp_c=45.0)
category = wbgt_risk_category(wbgt_val)

# Heat Index (Rothfusz NWS regression, Celsius input)
hi_val = heat_index(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0)
hi_val = heat_index_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
category = heat_index_risk_category(hi_val)

# Humidex (Canadian standard)
hx_val = humidex(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)

# Mean radiant temperature from solar radiation
tr = mean_radiant_temperature(temp_c=30.0, solar_rad_wm2=800.0, wind_ms=1.0)

# Wet bulb temperature
tw = wet_bulb_temperature(temp_c=35.0, rh=60.0)
tw = wet_bulb_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)

# Helpers
rh = relative_humidity_from_dewpoint(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0)
vp = vapor_pressure_from_dewpoint(dewpoint_c=25.0)

# Batch: compute all indices at once
results = calc_heat_indices(temp_c=35.0, dewpoint_c=25.0, wind_ms=2.0)
```

All functions accept scalar floats or numpy arrays. Temperature in Celsius, wind in m/s, humidity in %, radiation in W/m².

- UTCI (Bröde polynomial): params temp_c, rh, wind_ms, mrt_c.
- UTCI sparse (Roman et al. 2025, wider wind range 0.5-30.3 m/s): params temp_c, tmrt, wind_speed, rh.
- WBGT simple (Australian BoM approximation): params temp_c, dewpoint_c.
- WBGT shade (ISO 7243 indoor): params temp_c, wet_bulb_c.
- WBGT outdoor (ISO 7243): params temp_c, wet_bulb_c, globe_temp_c.
- Heat Index (Rothfusz NWS): params temp_c, rh.
- Humidex (Canadian standard): params temp_c, dewpoint_c.
- calc_heat_indices (all at once): params temp_c, dewpoint_c, wind_ms (optional), solar_rad_wm2 (optional).

### Spatial Analysis (`varunayan.spatial`)

```python
from varunayan import aggregate_to_polygons, check_grid_coverage, visualize_grid_overlap, compare_grids, get_polygon_timeseries

# Aggregate gridded data to polygon regions
result = aggregate_to_polygons(data=df, polygons=gdf, value_cols=["temperature"])

# Check how well a grid covers polygon boundaries
coverage = check_grid_coverage(grid_data=df, polygons=gdf)

# Time series for each polygon
ts = get_polygon_timeseries(data=df, polygons=gdf, value_col="temperature", time_col="time")

# Compare multiple grids (e.g., ERA5 vs IMD)
comparison = compare_grids(grids={"era5": df1, "imd": df2}, polygons=gdf)

# Visualize grid point overlap with polygons
visualize_grid_overlap(grid_data=df, polygons=gdf)
```

### Processing Utilities (`varunayan.processing`)

```python
from varunayan import categorize_variables, get_aggregation_method, is_sum_var, is_max_var, is_min_var, is_rate_var

method = get_aggregation_method("total_precipitation")  # returns "sum"
categorize_variables(["2m_temperature", "total_precipitation"])
```

Classifies ERA5 variables by their correct temporal aggregation method (sum, max, min, or mean).

### Cache Management (`varunayan.cache`)

```python
from varunayan import get_cache_dir, show_cache_info, list_cache, cache_stats, clear_cache, cache_exists, get_cached_data, save_to_cache, invalidate_cache

get_cache_dir()
show_cache_info()
df = list_cache(source="all")
stats = cache_stats()
clear_cache(source="all")
exists = cache_exists(source="era5", params={"variable": "2m_temperature"})
data = get_cached_data(source="era5", params={"variable": "2m_temperature"})
save_to_cache(data=df, source="era5", params={"variable": "2m_temperature"})
invalidate_cache(cache_key="abc123")
```

### CLI

The CLI provides ERA5 access via three subcommands: `geojson`, `bbox`, and `point`.

```
varunayan bbox --request-id demo --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-30 --north 28.7 --south 28.5 --east 77.3 --west 77.0
varunayan point --request-id pt --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-01 --lat 28.6 --lon 77.2
varunayan geojson --request-id geo --variables 2m_temperature --start 2023-06-01 --end 2023-06-30 --geojson region.geojson --dist-features state
```

Common flags: `--dataset-type` (single|pressure), `--pressure-levels` (comma-separated), `--freq` (hourly|daily|weekly|monthly|yearly), `--res` (grid resolution in degrees), `--verbosity` (0|1|2), `--save-raw` (true|false).

IMD, HadEX3, and CRU TS do not have CLI subcommands; use them via the Python API.
